<p>Agricultural advisory systems often need to combine current observations, earlier visits, and crop-disease knowledge, but existing agricultural benchmarks mainly evaluate image classification or short-form question answering. We present AgriMemSynth, a synthetic benchmark framework for evaluating agricultural question answering under two complementary requirements: multi-session conversational memory and structured multi-hop reasoning. AgriMemSynth provides AgriConvMem, a set of 500 generated advisory conversations, and AgriMultiHop, a set of 2,000 generated reasoning questions. Using held-out test splits with 146 conversational-memory questions and 200 multi-hop questions, we compare five retrieval organizations under a shared answer-generation pipeline: retrieval-augmented generation, a neuroscientific memory system, a hybrid retriever, BM25 with semantic reranking, and a graph-based memory system. Semantic evaluation reveals three stable benchmark patterns. First, lexical metrics substantially underestimate answer correctness. Second, conversational memory is harder than generated multi-hop reasoning. Third, retrieval organization is task-dependent: RAG has the highest conversational-memory score (85.6 %, 95 % CI: 79.0-90.4), whereas MemoryGraph has the highest multi-hop score (97.0 %, 95 % CI: 93.6-98.6). Temporal questions remain the weakest conversational category. These results support AgriMemSynth as a controlled benchmark for studying how agricultural AI systems organize, retrieve, and apply knowledge across longitudinal and relational relations in natural language is a crucial ability an intelligent system should possess. The bAbI dataset tries to capture tasks relevant to this domain (task 17 and 19). However, these tasks have several limitations. Most importantly, they are limited to fixed expressions, they are limited in the number of reasoning steps required to solve them, and they fail to test the robustness of models to input that contains irrelevant or redundant information. In this paper, we present a new Question-Answering dataset called StepGame for robust multi-step spatial reasoning in texts. Our experiments demonstrate that state-of-the-art models on the bAbI dataset struggle on the StepGame dataset. Moreover, we propose a Tensor-Product based Memory-Augmented Neural Network (TP-MANN) specialized for spatial reasoning tasks. Experimental results on both datasets show that our model outperforms all the baselines with superior generalization and robustness
